task.description: Idiom RE-GATE for ISS-0427 (Step 3c re-gate) after substantial implementation changes since the prior PASS: (1) normalize/3 -> normalize/2, fixing the parity check's structural blindness to a clone object repointed at the template (my own prior MAJOR is the reason this is now real rather than hollow); (2) index-name restoration (new mechanism step 3.5 plus a new, deliberately-ordered two-part parity dimension #4); (3) atomic build-then-rename-into-place for build_template!/0's crash safety. Judge idiom/quality of the new code including N+1 hunting (a possible fourth), the two-part dimension #4's real ordering and non-vacuity, whether my own prior MINOR (check_sequences N+1) was fixed, scope discipline, honesty of the twice-revised performance claim (2.5x expected -> 2.0x -> 1.79x median/1.74x average), and whether 1.79x still justifies the module's ~1300-1700 line complexity. Full suite reported 3208/3208, better than main's 3199/3200 -- judge the code, not the green result.

result.summary:
VERDICT: PASS. No BLOCKER. One MINOR carried forward as newly-confirmed-fixed (my own prior N+1), one NEW MINOR (a fourth N+1, deliberately accepted by the design as low-cost), one NEW MINOR (stale test narrative in tenant_template_test.exs), and my direct answer to the coordinator's real question on complexity-vs-payoff at the end. My prior MAJOR (assert_clone_parity!/2 wired nowhere) is CONFIRMED CLOSED -- re-derived independently, not taken on the coordinator's word: use site 1 now exists as assert_template_parity_against_independent_reference!/0 (opt-in via LETFLOW_TEMPLATE_REFCHECK, deliberately not unconditional -- see finding 6 below for why that is a sound tradeoff, not a backslide), and use site 2 now exists as test/support/tenant_template_test.exs, which I ran myself: `mix test test/support/tenant_template_test.exs` -> Result: 6 passed, exit 0, real Postgres, log confirms a genuine tenant_template vs tenant_template_refcheck two-schema comparison actually executing.

1. NORMALIZE/3 -> NORMALIZE/2, RE-DERIVED FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES, NOT TRUSTED. Read normalize/2 (tenant_template.ex:904-906) and every one of its 10 call sites directly (grep confirmed each: check_columns/2 passes reference_schema/candidate_schema to their own respective normalize_column_row/2 calls at the two separate map pipelines, lines 934-942; check_constraints/2 at lines 1006/1013 likewise differentiates; every def-fetching helper -- index_name_defs_by_table/1, index_name_defs/2, index_defs/1, trigger_defs/1, trigger_function_defs/1, statistics_ext_defs/1 -- takes exactly one schema_name and normalizes only against it). No call site reintroduces the old both-sides-stripped bug. The reasoning is sound and I verified it independently rather than re-quoting the handoff's own explanation: the old normalize/3 collapsed 'tenant_template.parents(id)' and 'tenant_abc.parents(id)' to the same string by stripping BOTH qualifiers from BOTH sides regardless of which side the text actually came from, which is exactly backwards -- the one piece of information that distinguishes a correct clone from a template-coupled one is which schema's name survives in the candidate's own text, and stripping the reference's qualifier out of the CANDIDATE text (which the old code did, since it stripped both patterns from both strings) destroys that exact signal. The fix strips only the schema each string was actually read from, so a residual 'tenant_template.' inside candidate text is never touched and shows up as a real diff. Confirmed non-vacuous by my own independent run of test/support/tenant_template_test.exs's tamper-and-detect tests (see above) plus by reading the concrete worked example test at lines 228-260, which the moduledoc documents was previously a false-pass under the old code and is now a real, correctly-attributed [dim #2] failure -- I re-derived that this is the right dimension to catch it at (the surviving qualifier shows up directly in the column DEFAULT text dimension #2 already compares, which is a stronger/earlier catch than dimension #5's structural pg_depend-based sequence-namespace check, which this specific tamper shape -- a plain SET DEFAULT with no change to sequence OWNED BY -- would not have reached at all).

2. THE TWO-PART DIMENSION #4 -- ORDERING VERIFIED, NOT MERELY CLAIMED. Read check_indexes/2 directly (lines 1061-1065): it is a flat two-statement function, structure_diffs = check_index_structure/2 (unconditional, always runs), then name_diffs = check_index_names/2 (its own, fully independent per-table structural pairing via a fresh Map.new(index_name_defs(...)) lookup, not fed any state from the structure check), then the two diff lists are concatenated. This is genuinely two separate passes, not a shared comparison with a name check bolted on -- confirmed by reading, not inferred from the comment. Non-vacuity confirmed via ELIXIR-DEV's own quoted proof (a real index renamed to a wrong name on a real clone raised '[dim #4] index name mismatch ... (structurally paired, def=...)') and independently re-confirmed by my own run of tenant_template_test.exs, which exercises the real clone-vs-template path end to end (though that file's own explicit index-name-mismatch tamper test was not enumerated in what I read of its describe blocks -- the FK/sequence/trigger tamper-and-detect tests I read directly at lines 100-311 are what I verified personally; ELIXIR-DEV's own quoted index-rename proof from the step-07 handoff is evidence I did not re-run myself, flagged here rather than silently inherited, but it is a real, quoted verbatim raised-message string, not a bare claim of success, which is the standard this project's anti-patterns doc asks for). The two never collapse into one combined match-then-compare -- confirmed structurally, which is what the design's own explicit anti-collapse instruction required.

3. MY OWN PRIOR MINOR (check_sequences/2 N+1) -- CONFIRMED FIXED. Read check_sequences/2 (lines 1165-1213) and its new serial_sequences_in/1 helper (lines 1223-1238) directly: discovery is now exactly one information_schema.columns-driven query per schema side (two total), returning a {table, column} => sequence map, with both sides' membership checked via Map.get/2 in-memory rather than a fresh round trip per column. Same batching technique already proven for recreate_sequences!/1. My prior finding is closed.

4. A FOURTH N+1 FOUND, PER THE COORDINATOR'S ASK -- IN check_index_names/2 (dimension #4(b), lines 1088-1119). It calls index_name_defs(schema, table) once per table per schema side inside its own Enum.flat_map(common_tables, ...) loop -- the exact per-table pg_indexes-query pattern the MECHANISM side (rename_indexes_to_template_names!/2) already had and fixed by batching into index_name_defs_by_table/1. This is real and I verified it by reading, not assuming. HOWEVER, unlike the three N+1s ELIXIR-DEV already found and fixed (all on the per-CLONE hot path, run 755+ times a suite), this one is on the PARITY-CHECK path, and the code's own comment at lines 666-671 states the reasoning for leaving it unbatched: it 'runs once per template build / once per dedicated parity test, not once per clone.' I verified this claim rather than accepting it: assert_clone_parity!/2 is invoked from exactly two places today -- the opt-in build-time refcheck (LETFLOW_TEMPLATE_REFCHECK=1, off by default) and test/support/tenant_template_test.exs's six tests, which I ran myself (6 passed, ~14.6s wall for the whole file including two full clone builds and several tamper-and-detects). At that call frequency (order of 10, not order of 1000+), an unbatched per-table query adds negligible absolute cost. This is a legitimate, deliberately-stated cost tradeoff, not an oversight -- filed as MINOR (informational) rather than something blocking, but flagged explicitly per the coordinator's ask so it does not go unrecorded, and because the same code (index_name_defs/2) would become a real problem if a future change wires check_index_names/2 onto a higher-frequency path without revisiting this note.

5. SCOPE. git diff main...HEAD -- lib/ is confined to lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md (2196 lines, a design doc, not application code) -- re-verified independently this pass, zero bytes changed in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex or any other lib/ file. ISS-0423's own scope (Sandbox.mode as a per-test async mechanism, genuine async: true adoption) is still not absorbed: the new Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call inside ensure_template!/0 (lines 69-82) is the SAME existing global :auto-mode idiom test/support/tenant_fixture.ex already established before this run (confirmed: identical call, same non-restoring rationale, grepped and compared both call sites directly) -- it is a defensive second call site for a pre-existing pattern (so ensure_template!/0 does not depend on TenantFixture having already set it), not new scope, not a step toward per-test async isolation. No absorption found.

6. HONESTY OF THE PERFORMANCE CLAIM (2.5x -> 2.0x -> 1.79x/1.74x), AND THE COORDINATOR'S REAL QUESTION ON WHETHER IT'S STILL WORTH THE COMPLEXITY. The arithmetic is sound: each downward revision is explained by a real, necessary, newly-added DDL cost (trigger/function re-add between step 3 and step 4 dropped 2.5x-expected to 2.0x-measured; index-rename between steps 3 and 4 dropped 2.0x to 1.79x/1.74x), not by an unexplained regression -- and ELIXIR-DEV's own report is honest in the specific way this project's anti-patterns doc asks for: it found and fixed an intermediate regression (per-table index discovery, 78 extra round trips, which had temporarily dropped the ratio to ~1.4x) BEFORE reporting a final number, rather than reporting the worse number as final or quietly reporting only the better one. I did not re-run the 10-run timing myself (this host's load is not controlled between sessions, and my own targeted test-file runs are not a substitute for that specific methodology), but the reported number's trajectory is internally consistent and each revision downward is causally tied to a real, verifiable code addition (trigger re-add exists, verified in my prior review; index rename exists, verified this review) rather than asserted. On the coordinator's real question -- is 1.79x still worth ~1700 lines of test infrastructure -- my independent view: YES, with one caveat. The module is not 1700 lines of incidental complexity; it is a 13-dimension structural-parity oracle plus a crash-safe build sequence, and the complexity is proportional to the actual hazard surface a naive LIKE-based clone has (FK loss, sequence-ownership leakage, trigger/function coupling, index/constraint-name loss, now independently proven to matter because it broke 7 real suite tests with raw Ecto.ConstraintError before this rework). A simpler clone mechanism with fewer fix-up steps would be faster to write but would either reintroduce one of these four now-proven-real hazards or would have to be re-discovered the hard way again, the way this run itself re-discovered the trigger and index-name gaps AFTER the original design's own repeated (and repeatedly wrong) dormancy claims. 1.79x is not a marginal win: it roughly halves per-schema provisioning cost, applied to (per ISS-0427's own filed estimate) several hundred provisionings a suite run -- a real, substantial, reproducible speedup even short of the original 2.5x target, and the honest reporting of each revision is itself evidence the number can be trusted rather than discounted further. The caveat: this module's own COST (not runtime cost -- maintenance cost) is now real and should be watched. It duplicates the same structural-pairing technique in three places (rename_indexes_to_template_names!/2, check_index_names/2, and index_defs/1's own structural_indexdef/1 helper) rather than sharing one implementation -- ELIXIR-DEV's own step-07 handoff flagged this exact duplication for my judgement. My judgement: acceptable as shipped (each site's own query shape differs enough -- one needs per-table grouped batches for the mechanism, one needs per-table pairing for the check -- that forcing a single shared function would add its own indirection cost), but if a FIFTH place needs the same pairing technique, that is the point to extract a shared helper rather than triple it a third time.

7. TEST COVERAGE. test/support/tenant_template_test.exs (429 lines, 6 tests, all independently re-run by me: 6 passed) covers design §3.4 use site 2 (full 13-dimension clone-vs-template parity) plus three of the four originally-planned tamper-and-detect non-vacuity proofs (FK missing, FK repointed-at-template, sequence-default repointed, trigger repointed-at-template -- I read all four directly). test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs covers the :clone-default/:replay-still-works dispatch contract I asked for in my prior review (finding 8(c)) -- confirmed present, not re-run in full this pass (out of this re-gate's scope, and it is unrelated to the three changes under review here). STILL MISSING, not blocking this PASS but worth naming for a follow-up: (a) no dedicated non-vacuity test for dimension #4(b) itself (index NAME mismatch) inside tenant_template_test.exs -- ELIXIR-DEV's own ad-hoc proof from the step-07 handoff is real evidence but is not committed, permanent test code, which is exactly the gap my own prior review's finding-8(a) asked TEST-DESIGNER to close for the OTHER three hazards and was closed for those three but not this fourth one; (b) no dedicated test proving build_template!/0's crash-safety property (INV-8: a crash before the ALTER SCHEMA RENAME leaves only inert staging debris, never a half-built 'tenant_template') as committed, permanent test code -- ELIXIR-DEV's own step-07 handoff describes a real, convincing fault-injection proof (a 1ms statement_timeout forcing a mid-build Postgrex error, confirmed no half-built schema survives) but, like the index-name case, it is an ad-hoc verification script, not permanent coverage. Recommend both as follow-up TEST-DESIGNER work, not as blockers on this gate -- the underlying mechanisms are independently proven correct by real fault injection and real tamper-and-detect runs (by ELIXIR-DEV for INV-8, by ELIXIR-DEV and indirectly by my own review for dimension #4(b)), just not yet captured as standing regression tests the way the other three hazards now are.

8. STALE TEST NARRATIVE FOUND (NEW MINOR). test/support/tenant_template_test.exs's describe-block comments at lines 129-140 and 180-227, plus two test NAMES themselves ('...fails dimension #3 -- CURRENTLY DOES NOT (MAJOR finding, see comment above)' at line 141, and the identical pattern at line 262 for dimension #8), narrate a MAJOR finding and reference '@tag :skip' as if both are still true today. Neither is: I grepped the file directly for the literal attribute '@tag :skip' and found ZERO real occurrences (only comment-text mentions of the phrase) -- the moduledoc's own line 20 correctly and currently states 'no @tag :skip' -- and I ran the file myself (6 passed), confirming both of these specific tests execute for real today and PASS, because normalize/2's fix (finding 1 above) already closed the exact gap they were written to document as open. This is not a correctness defect -- the tests run, and they pass for the right reason (the fix works) -- it is a documentation-staleness defect of the same class my own prior review flagged in template_self_check!/0's comment: a reader encountrering this file cold, without this run's full history, would be told by the test's own NAME and surrounding prose that a MAJOR gap still exists and is being deliberately skipped, when in fact it was fixed earlier in this same run. Recommend a small follow-up (test rename plus a one-line 'FIXED, see normalize/2' comment update) -- not routed as blocking since it is prose-only and the file's own moduledoc-level claim is accurate.

OVERALL: the three substantial changes since my last review are each independently sound, each closes a real hazard (a template-repointed clone escaping detection; a name-mismatched index breaking Ecto's error mapping in seven real tests; a crash mid-build permanently wedging a partition database), and the performance cost of the two newer mechanisms (triggers, index renames) is honestly measured and reasonably attributed rather than hidden or inflated. The complexity is proportional to real, demonstrated hazards, not speculative hardening -- my judgement is that 1.79x still justifies it.

issues.title: check_index_names/2 (parity dimension #4(b)) queries pg_indexes per table per schema side, the same N+1 shape already found and fixed three times elsewhere in this module (sequence discovery, check_sequences/2, and the index-rename mechanism itself) -- deliberately left unbatched here because the comment at tenant_template.ex:666-671 states, and I independently verified, that this check only runs on the order of 10 times per suite run (the opt-in build-time refcheck plus tenant_template_test.exs's own six tests), not on the per-clone hot path (755+ times a suite).
issues.description: Confirmed by reading check_index_names/2 (lines 1088-1119) directly and by running test/support/tenant_template_test.exs myself (6 passed, ~14.6s total including two full clone builds and several tamper-and-detects -- no timing red flag at this call frequency). Not blocking. If a future change wires assert_clone_parity!/2 (and thus dimension #4(b)) onto a higher-frequency path without revisiting this, batch index_name_defs/2 into a per-schema query the same way index_name_defs_by_table/1 already does for the mechanism side.

issues.title: test/support/tenant_template_test.exs's two dimension-#3/#8 'repointed at template' tests (names ending '-- CURRENTLY DOES NOT (MAJOR finding, see comment above)', lines 141 and 262) and their surrounding describe-block prose (lines 129-140, 180-227) describe a MAJOR finding and reference '@tag :skip' as current, but both were fixed by normalize/3 -> normalize/2 (this same run) and no '@tag :skip' attribute exists anywhere in the file (grepped directly, zero real occurrences -- only comment-text mentions) -- confirmed by running the file myself, 6/6 passed.
issues.description: Not a correctness defect: the tests run for real, pass for the right reason (normalize/2 genuinely fixed the hazard they test), and the file's own moduledoc (line 20) accurately states 'no @tag :skip'. It is a documentation-staleness defect in the test names and describe-block comments specifically, same class as the stale template_self_check!/0 comment my prior review (step-03c) flagged and which has since been corrected elsewhere in this same file -- these two spots were evidently missed when normalize/2 was fixed. A reader encountering this file without this run's full history would be told by the test's own name that a MAJOR gap is still open and deliberately skipped, when it is neither. Recommend renaming both tests (drop the '-- CURRENTLY DOES NOT' suffix) and updating the two comment blocks to state the fix and point at normalize/2, in a small follow-up -- not routed as blocking since this is prose-only and does not affect what the tests verify or whether they run.

result.next_action: Clear to proceed past this gate. Two MINOR follow-ups worth a small, low-priority follow-up task (not blocking merge): (1) rename/re-comment the two stale-narrative tests in test/support/tenant_template_test.exs per finding 8; (2) add permanent (not ad-hoc) regression tests for dimension #4(b) non-vacuity (index name mismatch) and build_template!/0's INV-8 crash-safety property, both currently proven only by ELIXIR-DEV's own un-committed verification scripts per finding 7. Neither blocks TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-RUNNER from proceeding on the green 3208/3208 suite.
